Treatment Plan:

3. Recommend lifestyle modifications including sun protection measures and regular exercise.
4. Referral to a rheumatologist for specialized care and long-term management.
5. Follow-up in the clinic in 4 weeks or sooner if symptoms worsen.

Patient Education:
The patient was directed to informative resources about lupus at https://www.lupus.org/resources and encouraged to join a local support group. She was also advised to contact the clinic if she experiences any side effects from the medications or notices new symptoms.

At the age of 76, Mr. Haruki Yamada was brought to the Emergency Department of Tokyo General Hospital on April 5, 2023, after experiencing a sudden onset of right-sided weakness and slurred speech. His wife, Keiko Yamada, reported that the symptoms began approximately 30 minutes before their arrival at the hospital.

Upon examination by the attending physician, Dr. Masaru Nakajima, it was suspected that Mr. Yamada was suffering from an acute ischemic stroke. Immediate orders were given for a CT scan of the brain to rule out any hemorrhagic components, and the stroke team was alerted of a possible thrombolytic therapy administration.

The CT scan confirmed the diagnosis of an acute ischemic stroke affecting the left middle cerebral artery territory without any signs of hemorrhage. After discussing the risks and benefits with Mrs. Yamada, alteplase (rt-PA) was administered intravenously within the therapeutic window of 4.5 hours from symptom onset.

Mr. Yamada was then transferred to the Stroke Unit for close monitoring and management. The following day, he showed signs of improvement with partial return of strength in his right side and clearer speech. A swallowing assessment was conducted by the speech and language therapist, and a soft diet was introduced under supervision.

On April 7, 2023, a brain MRI was performed, which revealed the extent of the infarct and ruled out any additional areas of ischemia. The multidisciplinary team, including neurologists, physical therapists, occupational therapists, and nutritionists, devised a comprehensive rehabilitation plan for Mr. Yamada's recovery.

Throughout his stay, Mr. Yamada's condition continued to improve. He engaged actively in rehabilitation sessions and regained more function on his right side. His speech became clearer, and he was able to express his needs effectively. The medical team, led by Dr. Nakajima, adjusted his medications to include antihypertensive drugs, a statin, and an antiplatelet agent to manage risk factors and prevent future stroke events.

After two weeks of intensive inpatient rehabilitation, Mr. Yamada was discharged on April 19, 2023, with a plan for ongoing outpatient therapy and follow-up appointments with the neurology clinic. Mrs. Yamada expressed her gratitude to the staff at Tokyo General Hospital for the excellent care her husband received during his stay.
